title: Sliding Window
intuition: Maintains a running calculation over a moving contiguous subsegment to eliminate redundant computation.
whyExists: Finding optimal subarrays (maximum sum, longest unique substring) without recalculating from scratch for every window.
analogy: A magnifying glass sliding across a tape measure: as it slides right, you only look at what enters on the right and what leaves on the left.
coreIdea: Instead of recalculating a window sum of size $k$ in $O(k)$ time for each of the $n$ positions ($O(n \cdot k)$), the window slides by adding the incoming element a[i] and subtracting the departing element a[i - k] in $O(1)$ operations.

complexity.reason: Each element enters the window once and exits the window once.

pitfalls: Window size k larger than array length n without validation.
Off-by-one errors when subtracting the departing element (a[i - k] vs a[i - k + 1]).
Failing to track window boundaries accurately when window size is dynamic.
